name: AOI01 Chibabel: Chókwè, Macia and Xai-Xai, Mozambique

reference.product: Delineation (DEL), monitoring 0, version 1, scored only where it agrees with the First Estimate Product (FEP) from Sentinel-1 at 16:22 UTC on 16 Jan (observed 20,126.9 ha)

method.name: lightgbm
method.summary: LightGBM classifier on 14 radar features (HH, HV, HV minus HH, the change between dates, and 5x5 local mean and spread), each with the area's median over land with no water on record (JRC 0%) removed; flood where the probability is at least 0.36; not water on 5 Jan (DSWx-S1, or JRC occurrence >= 4% where DSWx-S1 has no data); not permanent water (JRC occurrence >= 50%).

aoi05_test.decision_rule: higher AOI05 IoU at 3 decimals wins; a tie keeps the rule

post_fix_rerun.label: post-fix rerun
post_fix_rerun.note: Not a clean test. The land-median fix was found on AOI01 after AOI05 had been used as the test. The clean held-out figure is the v1 score in test_lgbm_vs_rule.json.
post_fix_rerun.decided_before_scoring: The fix stays whatever this number is. The method choice is reopened only if LightGBM falls below the tuned rule's AOI05 IoU of 0.521 (at 3 decimals).

legend.2: #bdbdbd at alpha 170: valid, outside the area both Copernicus maps cover, or where the 16 and 18 Jan maps disagree
legend.3: #e6ab02 at alpha 170: unclear: HH rose, possible flooded vegetation
legend.4: #7570b3 at alpha 170: edge buffer, not scored

limits: NISAR Beta data: not fully calibrated. The 17 Jan scene is about 3 dB brighter overall, so each area's median over land with no water on record (JRC 0%) is removed before the classifier sees it.

Agreement with Copernicus, not accuracy, and a lower bound: no Copernicus map was made on the NISAR morning here. The reference maps are from about 11 hours before (Sentinel-1, C-band) and 35 hours after (COSMO-SkyMed, X-band) the NISAR pass, so part of their difference may be the sensor, not the flood.

The Beta data on ascending track 114 ends on 17 Jan 03:42 UTC, and as of 13 Nov 2026 the next pass in the catalogue is 22 June. Copernicus observed a larger flood here on 20 Jan (127,755.1 ha), after that pass.
Pixels where HH rose by more than 3 dB (possible flooded vegetation) are not scored. This method only finds open water.
Permanent water (JRC occurrence >= 50%) is never counted as flood.
A 2-pixel band along the Copernicus mapped-area edge is not scored. Flood polygon edges are scored.
The classifier learned from the Copernicus map of AOI06 only.

Only pixels where both maps agree are scored. They disagree on 37% of the area both cover (mostly flooded on 18 Jan only), and those pixels count as outside the mapped area. The red overlay shows flood on both maps (17,569 ha on this grid), not the full 18 Jan extent.
DSWx-S1 covers only 32% of this area on 5 Jan. Elsewhere, water before the flood is JRC occurrence >= 4%, the level that best matches DSWx-S1 where both exist (IoU 0.38).

On the held-out area AOI05, the tuned rule scored IoU 0.521 and LightGBM 0.572 against Copernicus, so the LightGBM classifier is used. That is the one clean test. A fix to how the land median is taken was found later, on AOI01, and AOI05 was scored once more after it (a post-fix rerun, not a clean test): IoU 0.574.

Against this area's reference, LightGBM scores IoU 0.835. This is a diagnostic, not a test score: the land-median problem was found on this area. Before the fix LightGBM scored 0.718 here, and the tuned rule scores 0.833. The method was chosen on AOI05, not here.

About 44% of the detected new water (33,787 ha of 75,951 ha) lies outside both Copernicus maps, with no independent check. A further 10% (7,802 ha) is covered only by the 18 Jan map, so it is not scored either.

Some of the new water north-west of Xai-Xai may be irrigation, not flood: 2,622 ha (23 buildings) lies in the field grids there, and about 525 ha of it was already dark in NISAR's 5 Jan image. Downstream of Chókwè, 7,799 ha (81 buildings) lies in a field grid, but the evidence leans towards flood water held in the fields, not irrigation: where the 18 Jan COSMO-SkyMed map covers it, the map calls most of it flooded, and JRC has almost never seen water there. This is not confirmed. The optical image of 19 Jan (HLS) is cloud-covered, so it could not settle either area.
13,174 ha (17%) of the detected new water was already dark in NISAR's 5 Jan image. DSWx-S1 (or JRC) called it dry, so it counts as new, but some of it may have been water before 17 Jan.

Buildings: 824 OpenStreetMap buildings sit inside detected new water, out of 346,003 mapped on this grid. For this area the count is about 680 to 820 mapped buildings in detected water, depending on method. The count can be too high or too low. Too low: OpenStreetMap is incomplete here, and flooded built-up areas look bright in radar, so open-water detection misses them. Too high: a 30 m pixel is larger than a house, so a building beside water can fall on a water pixel, and some detected water may not be flood. It says nothing about damage. Data: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
